articles.title: Listing Writer: a private AI that writes product listings for small sellers
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle Listing Writer is a small web app that turns a few product facts into a ready-to-post online listing. You type t…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built Listing Writer is a small web app that turns a few product facts into a ready-to-post online listing. You type the product name, a few key details (materials, size, colour, what makes it special), the price, where you'll post it (Etsy, eBay, Instagram or WhatsApp Business), and the tone you want. It returns a title, a description of about 100 words, six tags, and a short caption with the price. Who would pay for it? Small sellers: home bakers, craft makers, boutique owners and anyone selling on Instagram or WhatsApp. They know their products well but spend a lot of time writing descriptions, and many are not confident writing in English.

articles.body: How Do AI Agents on Different Computers Talk to Each Other? I Built a Tiny Open-Source Fix ACP-lite (Agent Connect Personal) v0.7.0 is out: https://github.com/furoute/acp-lite Note: unrelated to Zed's Agent Client Protocol and OpenAI+Stripe's Agentic Commerce Protocol — same acronym, different project. The problem I run 6 AI agents across 3 machines: Codex and DSH on my desktop, Hermes and OpenClaw on a netbook. Human-to-agent is easy — WeChat, DingTalk, done. But how do agents talk to each other ? Search for answers and you get enterprise stacks: Google's A2A, RabbitMQ, Kafka. All built for data centers. My need is much smaller: two home computers, both behind NAT, no public IP, no server — agents passing messages and tasks to each other. Nobody builds for that.

articles.excerpt: Subnetting is an important networking skill for IT students and people preparing for certifications such as the CCNA Subnetting is an important networking skill for IT students and people preparing fo…
articles.body: Subnetting is an important networking skill for IT students and people preparing for certifications such as the CCNA Subnetting is an important networking skill for IT students and people preparing for certifications such as the CCNA. It helps you understand how IP addresses are grouped into networks. In this tutorial, we'll work through an IPv4 /26 subnet example step by step. 1. What does /26 mean? The /26 is a CIDR prefix. It means that 26 of the 32 bits in an IPv4 address identify the network. The subnet mask for /26 is 255.255.255.192. Each /26 subnet contains 64 total IP addresses. Traditionally, two addresses are reserved for the network address and broadcast address, leaving 62 usable host addresses in a conventional IPv4 subnet. 2.

articles.title: Your First HIPAA App: 8 Things Developers Learn the Hard Way
articles.excerpt: Your first healthcare project usually starts with a familiar feature list: forms, a dashboard, messaging, search. You have built all of these before. Then someone says "HIPAA" on the kickoff call, and…
articles.body: Your first healthcare project usually starts with a familiar feature list: forms, a dashboard, messaging, search. You have built all of these before. Then someone says "HIPAA" on the kickoff call, and the familiar list stops feeling familiar. HIPAA is the US law that protects health information. For developers, most of it lands in two places. The Privacy Rule limits who can see and share patient data. The Security Rule sets the safeguards your system needs around electronic patient data. There is no official HIPAA certification for software. Compliance is something you build and document, not a badge you earn. It applies when your app handles health data for a healthcare provider, a health plan, or a vendor working for them. A standalone fitness tracker may fall outside it.

articles.title: Sony just proved that ‘three OS updates’ doesn’t really mean anything
articles.excerpt: Sony needs to offer a much stronger explanation for this.
articles.body: TL;DR Sony has decided not to roll out the Android 17 update to the Xperia 10 VI. The company says it’s due to “technical limitations” of the Xperia 10 VI’s storage configuration. The Xperia 10 VI was promised three OS updates at launch, implying that it would be upgraded to Android 17. Sony started rolling out Android 17 to its flagship Xperia 1 VIII early last month. At the same time, the company released a list of phones eligible for the update, which surprisingly did not include the Xperia 10 VI. While that raised doubts about Sony’s plans for the phone, we now know that it’s simply never getting Android 17 . In a notice posted on its website, Sony confirmed that the Xperia 10 VI, released in 2024, will not be updated to Android 17.

articles.excerpt: Gary Larson's comic strip The Far Side was known for its visual humor, but this is the best-ever quote from the series
articles.body: Larson didn’t do deep . He didn’t do inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful in the lofty sense. They required thought because Larson’s work was brilliant, and you sometimes had to figure out what the punchline was. For example, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly on his glasses. Larson’s work often requires the reader to investigate something, but usually not in any kind of overly deep way.

articles.body: Every once in a while, I come across a line that feels bigger than the book that birthed it. But few are quite as elegant or as profoundly humanistic as the final moments of Arkady and Boris Strugatsky’s Roadside Picnic . The 1972 novel offers a very different kind of sci-fi ending than its myriad predecessors and successors.

articles.body: Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads with zero-click exploits that installed sophisticated malware on the devices of targeted individuals when they did nothing other than load a website or open an installed app. The finding, published Thursday by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, said the incident is likely to be the first confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads. The attacks, which worked on iOS and Android devices, are particularly pernicious because they work without requiring any interaction from the target and are invisible unless users run special forensic hardware or software.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars’ Moons in Upcoming Mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long his…
articles.body: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample of Phobos to Earth. The MMX spacecraft is targeting launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan at 3:41 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 19 (4:41 a.m. JST on Tuesday, Oct. 20). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars’ orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 .
